digest.component_or_area: tickets-store reconciler and bridge state cache
propositions: The tickets branch is 1.04 GiB with 92% occupied by the reconciler's .bridge_state cache; the committed bindings.json is 18 MB and exhibits 7.4x marginal packed-size reduction by removing the baseline_advanced_at timestamp field which is written but never read in src/

The baseline_advanced_at field (1144 entries changed per pass) and last_get_pass rotation bookkeeping (20 changes per pass) cause scattered edits that defeat git delta compression, with measured marginal cost of 12.79 KB per version that reduces to 1.74 KB after timestamp deletion

The reconciler runs on ephemeral GitHub runners and requires durable state in git; the solution keeps .bridge_state committed while reducing churn by deleting unused bookkeeping fields and moving last_get_pass to a separate get_rotation.json sidecar with mixed-version read compatibility

A one-time history rewrite using git fast-export/filter/fast-import reduces the existing branch from 1.17 GB to 98.8 MB (8.4% of original) while preserving all 49,888 commits and 2,661 merges and restoring an identical HEAD tree

Two consecutive reconciler passes over unchanged Jira state must produce byte-identical bindings.json with no new commit, and rebar reconcile-check against pre-migration stores must leave the worktree byte-identical
Post-rewrite writers must demonstrate fail-closed epoch-mismatch refusal at both sync._union_merge and push.py non-FF retry sites, with no force bypasses used in ordinary clients
